subject.title: Crestodian chat hijacks natural language into operations; approvals require a literal hardcoded yes

question: Should Crestodian adopt the AI-first chat boundary from the open candidate PR, and what explicit approval boundary must remain before chat-driven setup or other state-changing operations?
rationale: Current source proves the bug, but the fix changes deterministic parsing, host approval intent, channel setup/directive handoffs, stale proposal state, and sensitive-history handling across setup and security boundaries.

options.title: Revise the candidate PR
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100656 as the fix path, but require it to preserve approval/security contracts and add real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to safety first
options.body: Ship an anchored-parser and approval-intent hotfix first, then track directives, executor refactor, and Gemini parity separately.

options.title: Split the umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue canonical but require separate maintainer-owned follow-ups for parser safety, approval intent, stale proposals, secret redaction, executor refactor, and Gemini parity.

recommendation.title: Revise the candidate PR
recommendation.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100656 as the fix path, but require it to preserve approval/security contracts and add real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Crestodian feature history and the open candidate fix both point to steipete as the best available product and security-boundary owner.
